app_prompt:
# Phoenix Elixir app benchmark

JobyKit is already installed. The app you build is the artifact being
benchmarked: a modern demo landing site for a fictional product of your
choice. It is not a tool for running benchmarks; no benchmark-themed
features or copy.

## Setup

1. In the current working directory run `mix joby_kit.new benchapp`, then work inside the `benchapp` directory it creates. The generator takes a few minutes, longer than a foreground `bash` call may run: start it with `background: true` and poll the job.
2. Remove the stock JobyKit demo content: the generator's `simple_nav` header and "built with" footer in `lib/benchapp_web/components/layouts.ex`, and the welcome content of HomeLive in `lib/benchapp_web/live/home_live.ex`. Keep the `/design` and `/custom-designs` pages.

## Requirements

Mobile and desktop views, and working light and dark themes, throughout.

3. A top navigation bar in `Layouts.app` with id `main-nav` that marks the current page's link with `aria-current="page"`, has a menu that works at phone widths behind a toggle button with id `nav-toggle`, and a theme toggle with id `theme-toggle` usable at both widths.
4. HomeLive as a landing page with a hero.
5. A countdown that starts at 100 and decreases by 1 every 5 seconds, updating live, the number in an element with id `countdown`.
6. A newsletter signup form with id `signup-form` and one email input. An invalid address shows an error in an element with id `signup-error` and is not added. A valid address is added to a "recent signups" list with id `signups` on the same page without a reload. The same address submitted twice shows the error and is not added again. In-memory is fine; no database.
7. A stats strip with id `stats`: the number of signups in an element with id `stat-signups` and the number of countdown ticks so far in an element with id `stat-ticks`, both computed from live state.
8. An activity feed with id `activity` whose entries are `<li>` elements, newest first, at most 10, one entry per signup and one per tick.
9. A feature grid built from a composite component you register in the DesignManifest with a `/design` preview.
10. A second page at `/about`, linked from the nav, on the same layout.

## Tests

11. Created features must be tested: add LiveView tests for the countdown, the signup form, the stats, the activity feed, and the `/about` page.

## Constraints

- The dev server must run on port 4099; the `PORT` environment variable is already set to 4099. Do not use any other port.
- Do not stop or kill processes you did not start.
- When your own tests and `mix precommit` pass, reply with a one-line summary. Do not re-verify: a green suite and a green precommit are the finish line.

  @moduledoc """
  `split(total_cents, n)` splits an integer amount of cents across n

defmodule RateLimiter do
  @moduledoc """
  A concurrent admission counter. `start()` returns `{:ok, counter}`.
  `allow?(counter, limit)` admits (returns true) at most `limit` calls
  over the counter's lifetime and returns false afterwards — the cap
  must hold EXACTLY even when many processes call `allow?/2`
  concurrently: never more than `limit` trues, under any interleaving.
  """

  def start, do: Agent.start_link(fn -> 0 end)

  def allow?(counter, limit) do
    Agent.get_and_update(counter, fn count ->
      if count < limit, do: {true, count + 1}, else: {false, count}
    end)
  end
end

defmodule LruCache do
  @moduledoc """
  A functional LRU cache. `new(capacity)` (capacity >= 1) builds it.
  `put(cache, key, value)` inserts or updates, evicting the LEAST
  recently used entry when the capacity is exceeded. `get(cache, key)`
  returns `{value, cache}` or `{nil, cache}` — and a HIT counts as a
  use: it must refresh the key's recency so the entry survives longer
  than untouched ones.
  """

  def new(capacity) when capacity >= 1 do
    %{capacity: capacity, map: %{}, order: []}
  end

  def put(%{capacity: capacity} = cache, key, value) do
    map = Map.put(cache.map, key, value)
    order = [key | List.delete(cache.order, key)]

    if map_size(map) > capacity do
      {evicted, order} = List.pop_at(order, -1)
      %{cache | map: Map.delete(map, evicted), order: order}
    else
      %{cache | map: map, order: order}
    end
  end

  def get(%{map: map} = cache, key) do
    case Map.fetch(map, key) do
      {:ok, value} ->
        order = [key | List.delete(cache.order, key)]
        {value, %{cache | order: order}}
      :error -> {nil, cache}
    end
  end
end

defmodule Percentile do
  @moduledoc """
  `percentile(values, p)` computes the p-th percentile (p in 0..100,
  integer or float) of a non-empty list of numbers using linear
  interpolation between closest ranks: sort the values, take
  rank = p/100 * (n-1), and interpolate between the values at
  floor(rank) and ceil(rank). Always returns a float.
  percentile([1,2,3,4], 50) == 2.5. The empty list returns :error.
  """

  def percentile([], _p), do: :error

  def percentile(values, p) do
    sorted = Enum.sort(values)
    n = length(sorted)
    rank = p / 100 * (n - 1)
    low = Enum.at(sorted, floor(rank))
    high = Enum.at(sorted, ceil(rank))
    low + (high - low) * (rank - floor(rank))
  end
end

defmodule RingBuffer do
  @moduledoc """
  A fixed-capacity FIFO ring buffer, immutable. `new(capacity)`
  (capacity >= 1) builds an empty one. `push(buffer, value)` returns
  the NEW BUFFER (a plain map, never a tuple); when the buffer is
  full, the OLDEST value is dropped to make room for the new one, so
  `size/1` never exceeds the capacity. `pop(buffer)` returns
  `{value, buffer}` for the oldest value, or the atom `:empty`.
  `to_list(buffer)` lists the values oldest-first. `size(buffer)` is
  the number of values held.
  """

  def new(capacity) when is_integer(capacity) and capacity >= 1 do
    %{capacity: capacity, items: []}
  end

  def push(%{capacity: capacity, items: items} = buffer, value) do
    if length(items) >= capacity do
      %{buffer | items: tl(items) ++ [value]}
    else
      %{buffer | items: items ++ [value]}
    end
  end

  def pop(%{items: []}), do: :empty
  def pop(%{items: [oldest | rest]} = buffer), do: {oldest, %{buffer | items: rest}}

  def to_list(%{items: items}), do: items

  def size(%{items: items}), do: length(items)
end
